args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. The plan was to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent healthy production release, but the rollback was rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined for CVE-2026-4417. checkout-api was instead rolled back to v2.2.9, the next most recent healthy production release, in all regions. After the rollback, the service is healthy with a 0.2% error rate. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, confirm whether v2.2.9 is affected by CVE-2026-4417, and prepare a fixed release.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to **v2.2.9** in all regions instead of v2.3.0. The service is healthy again, and SEV2 incident INC-0001 is open.

- **Why not v2.3.0:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, but the system rejected the rollback because that version is blocked over a security vulnerability (CVE-2026-4417). Nothing changed on that attempt.
- **Rollback:** v2.2.9 is the next most recent healthy production release, and it isn't blocked. It's now running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The service passes health checks again, and the error rate fell from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is a SEV2 for checkout-api, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It explains that v2.3.1 failed (its pre-release build had also failed in staging), why v2.3.0 was skipped, and that the service is now on v2.2.9.

**Follow-up needed:** I haven't checked whether v2.2.9 is also affected by CVE-2026-4417. The system didn't block it, but that should be confirmed. That check, finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and preparing a fixed release are listed as follow-ups in the incident.
